title: Playing the White House Rose Garden in 1976
summary: The World's Greatest Jazz Band plays for President Ford's Bicentennial salute alongside Ella Fitzgerald, and Leeman recalls his western outfit in the photograph.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Among other credits in the World's Greatest Jazz Band, and one of the things that I am most proud of, I just went in my living room and brought back a plaque, and the plaque was sent from the White House in Washington, D.C. I must read what it says: It says, "Dear Mr. Leeman, Mrs. Ford and I were delighted that our guests had such an enjoyable evening in the White House Rose Garden, on July 20th. A Salute To American Music was certainly enthusiastically applauded by everyone present, and the World's Greatest Jazz Band made a splendid contribution to the program. As one of the talented members of this outstanding group, your participation added a great deal to our pleasure on this occasion. You have our warm thanks and very best wishes, sincerely ..." and it is signed by hand, it says Jerry Ford and Betty Ford.
That stemmed from a command performance. We were asked at the White House, and it was for a Centennial of American Music, which also pertains to these archives at the Rose Garden, 1976.
When I say 'pertaining' to the archives, I meant that
I was told that our performance was recorded at this time in the Rose Garden, and was to be included in the archives of -- the Presidential archives.

I have to add that Ella Fitzgerald was on that bill with us, and above the plaque that I just mentioned, there was a picture sent from President Ford, and was taken of he and his wife, Betty, with the Lawson-Haggard band, and it's rather humorous because everybody comments on it, everybody was in tuxedos and the President was in full tails, except myself, and the reason for that is after our performance, not knowing we were to be photographed with the President, I changed my clothes; I was wringing wet as usual, and to the uninitiated, I wore western clothes, and for reasons which I'll get to later on -- I have for years, and I had a very flamboyant western sports suit, it was light tan in color, my pride and joy, llama boots, yellow with a very pointed toe. The picture is in color.

And, with my western shirt and pearl buttons, I did -- when they told us we were having pictures taken, I put on a black bow tie. I really wish since -- it turned out so ridiculous that I wished I had a ten-gallon hat to go with it, for the picture. However, the picture is for posterity, and here it is, as it was taken.
Oh yes -- my predominant huge silver belt buckle with my Odessa sherrif's department badge rounded out the picture. I think I looked pretty good!
When the wonderful, great piano player, Ralph Sutton, visited my house, he looked at the picture and commented, "Where were your sixguns, Cliff?" and I said "Security wouldn't allow me".
